questions.stem: Day surgery is a planned procedure or investigation with discharge within ____.
What is the 30-day perioperative mortality after day surgery?
What is the 30-day perioperative mortality after cataract surgery?
What does day surgery emphasise as a key principle?
questions.answer: Efficiency and throughput

questions.stem: What does the SAMBA S.A.F.E. principle recommend for day surgery anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Short-acting, fast-emergence anaesthesia

questions.stem: What do the 4 As stand for in the day surgery key principles?
questions.answer: Alertness, analgesia, ambulation, alimentation

questions.stem: For day surgery selection, which surgical question checks inpatient needs?
questions.answer: Will the operation need inpatient monitoring or care?

questions.stem: What operation duration is best for day surgery, though there is no absolute cut-off?
Day surgery suits procedures with a low risk of serious ____.
questions.answer: complications

questions.stem: For day surgery, what pain level suits the patient, and how is it managed?
questions.answer: Low pain, managed with oral or rectal analgesia and local techniques, little opioid

questions.stem: For day surgery selection, what must be true about postoperative needs?
questions.answer: They can be met at home

questions.stem: In day surgery selection, what can happen to a minor procedure in a complex patient?
questions.answer: It may still need admission

questions.stem: Name the previous anaesthetic problems that matter in day surgery patient selection.
questions.answer: Difficult airway, PONV, postoperative cognitive dysfunction, poor pain control

questions.stem: What should be assessed for children being considered for day surgery?
questions.answer: Risk factors for postoperative apnoea

questions.stem: In day surgery, which PCA cut-off applies to term infants under 1 month?
In day surgery, under what PCA are ex-preterm infants considered at risk?
Ex-preterm infants with a haematocrit under ____% are at higher risk in day surgery.
How long must infants on a home apnoea monitor be apnoea-free before day surgery?
Which age independently predicts admission and death after day surgery?
Which types of surgery are unsuitable for day surgery?
questions.answer: Airway surgery, tonsillectomy in children under 3 years, upper abdominal surgery

questions.stem: At what age is tonsillectomy unsuitable for day surgery in children?
What BMI defines morbid obesity when judging day surgery suitability?
Does obesity alone exclude a patient from day surgery?
questions.answer: No, look at complications; obesity alone may not exclude

questions.stem: For day surgery, how long should a responsible carer ideally stay with the patient?
How soon must a day surgery patient be able to reach hospital?
What must a day surgery patient be willing to do?
questions.answer: Go home the same day

questions.stem: Ideally, where and when should day surgery preoperative assessment happen?
questions.answer: In a preoperative clinic well before surgery

questions.stem: What are the goals of the preoperative assessment for day surgery?
questions.answer: Routine fitness assessment and optimisation, suitability for day surgery, and education on the day surgery pathway

questions.stem: How should preoperative testing be chosen for day surgery?
Why should sedative premedication be avoided where possible in day surgery?
options: Prolongs recovery, especially after short cases

questions.stem: What oral paracetamol dose is given for pre-emptive analgesia in day surgery?
What oral diclofenac dose is given for pre-emptive analgesia in day surgery?
When does pre-emptive oral analgesia in day surgery reach peak effect?
Which anaesthetic techniques all allow quick discharge in day surgery?
questions.answer: GA, regional, combined, and monitored sedation

questions.stem: Which monitoring may help avoid overdose and slow recovery in day surgery?
Which induction agent is preferred over thiopental for day surgery?
What advantage do volatile agents offer for emergence in day surgery?
For volatile anaesthesia in day surgery, at what MAC is awareness less likely?
In day-surgery anaesthesia, which muscle relaxant can cause myalgia that delays return to normal activity?
Which type of muscle relaxant is preferred in day-surgery anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Short-acting (e.g. mivacurium, atracurium)

questions.stem: In day-surgery anaesthesia, what IV fluid volume reduces PONV and dizziness and speeds recovery?
Why use multimodal analgesia in day-surgery patients?
questions.answer: To cut opioid need and its side effects (sedation, PONV, respiratory depression)

questions.stem: What paracetamol dose is given PR or IV for day-surgery analgesia?
Which NSAID is given PR or IV at 1mg/kg for day-surgery analgesia?
In day surgery, above what morphine dose per kg do admission rates rise?
questions.answer: Over 0.1mg/kg

questions.stem: Which opioids are short-acting options for day-surgery analgesia?
questions.answer: Remifentanil, alfentanil, fentanyl

questions.stem: Which NMDA antagonist is a low-dose analgesic adjunct in day-surgery analgesia?
Why does postoperative nausea and vomiting matter in day surgery?
questions.answer: A leading cause of delayed discharge and unplanned admission

questions.stem: What preoperative fluid fast length does the day-surgery PONV section recommend?
questions.answer: 2h

questions.stem: For day-surgery PONV prevention, which drug class is a reasonable single agent for most patients?
Which day-surgery PONV drugs sedate less than droperidol, prochlorperazine or promethazine?
questions.answer: Scopolamine patch, low-dose dexamethasone, 5HT3 antagonists and metoclopramide

questions.stem: For day-surgery spinal anaesthesia, which needle reduces post-dural puncture headache risk?
In day-surgery low-dose spinal anaesthesia, what bupivacaine dose is typically used?
In day-surgery low-dose spinal anaesthesia, what fentanyl dose is added to the local anaesthetic?
How long does an epidural block take to establish, making it less suitable for day surgery?
Which additive at 1mcg/kg prolongs a caudal block up to 24h in day surgery?
For a day-surgery caudal block, what dilute bupivacaine concentration is given as an example?
In local anaesthesia with sedation for day surgery, sedation does not rescue a poor ____.
questions.answer: block

questions.stem: For day-surgery sedation, what propofol target concentration is suggested for TCI?
What IV midazolam dose is given as boluses for day-surgery sedation?
What remifentanil infusion rate is used for day-surgery sedation with local anaesthesia?
In local anaesthesia with sedation for day surgery, who should give and monitor the sedation?
options: A dedicated person other than the surgeon

questions.stem: In day surgery, what are the two commonest causes of delayed discharge?
questions.answer: Pain and ongoing nausea or vomiting (with poor oral intake)

questions.stem: In day-surgery recovery, what active issues are managed in Phase I?
questions.answer: BP, pain, hypoxia

questions.stem: What does fast-tracking in day surgery do with Phase I recovery?
questions.answer: Bypasses it, going from theatre straight to Phase II

questions.stem: What modified Aldrete score must most day-surgery patients exceed in theatre for fast-tracking?
questions.answer: over 12

questions.stem: What are the advantages of home continuous peripheral nerve blocks after day surgery?
questions.answer: Sustained analgesia, opioid-sparing, better rehabilitation, fewer recovery and unplanned admissions

questions.stem: What are the drawbacks of home continuous peripheral nerve blocks after day surgery?
questions.answer: Numb limb at home, catheter migration, local anaesthetic toxicity, infection

questions.stem: For home nerve catheters after day surgery, how long must anaesthetic services be accessible?
What safety measures are needed for home continuous nerve blocks after day surgery?
questions.answer: Dilute solution, careful selection, 24h access to anaesthetic services, clear written and verbal instructions, daily phone follow-up

questions.stem: Which criteria must still be met before discharge home after day surgery?
questions.answer: Stable airway, breathing, circulation and consciousness; surgical issues settled; pain and PONV controlled

questions.stem: What pain control is needed before discharge home after day surgery?
questions.answer: Reasonable pain control on oral drugs

questions.stem: What must a patient do before discharge home after day surgery?
questions.answer: Tolerate oral intake without vomiting

questions.stem: After day surgery, which patients at high risk of urinary retention should void before discharge?
What two arrangements are essential for a day-surgery patient going home?
questions.answer: Escort home and carer at home

questions.stem: After day surgery, what share of patients may have moderate to severe pain at home?
How long can moderate to severe pain at home last after day surgery?
How long after day surgery should patients avoid driving or cycling?
In day-surgery follow-up, on which day is the follow-up phone call made?
Which preoperative factors delay discharge after day surgery?
questions.answer: Female sex, older age, heart failure

questions.stem: Which postoperative factors delay discharge after day surgery?
questions.answer: PONV, pain, drowsiness, no escort

questions.stem: Which surgical problems cause unplanned admission after day surgery?
questions.answer: Pain, bleeding, surgical complications, need for more extensive surgery

questions.stem: Which anaesthetic problems cause unplanned admission after day surgery?
questions.answer: PONV, drowsiness or dizziness, cognitive dysfunction, cardiovascular events, laryngospasm, aspiration
